[ASSISTANT_SAID] Neem oil is an effective insecticide and repellent; it should be diluted in water and sprayed onto affected plants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Garlic has natural insect-repellent properties; it can be mixed with water and sprayed onto plants or used to create a barrier around plants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Diatomaceous earth is a natural insecticide made from fossilized diatoms; it can be spread around plant beds or directly on plants to kill pests like snails.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting with certain plants, such as marigolds, can repel pests while attracting beneficial insects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Beer traps can lure slugs and snails; a shallow dish or container should be buried in the soil and filled with beer.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A soap and water solution can be a powerful insecticide for aphids; it should be made with a few drops of soap mixed with water and sprayed onto affected plants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Organic mulch can deter pests by creating a barrier between the soil and plants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Prevention is key in dealing with garden pests; encouraging beneficial insects, practicing good hygiene, and using physical barriers like netting are recommended.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The beer trap can be effective for snail control; it is advised to empty and refill the container with fresh beer regularly.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] While the beer trap is designed to attract snails and slugs, it may also attract other insects; it is recommended to regularly check the trap and remove any non-target insects.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The soap and water solution is a great natural remedy for aphids; a mild soap should be used, and a small area of the plant should be tested before treating the whole plant.
